title: Most Recent Order Per Customer Using LATERAL JOIN
description:
For each customer retrieve only their single most recent order using a LATERAL (correlated) join.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `customer_name`, `order_date`, `amount`. Order by `customer_name`.
solution_sql: SELECT c.name AS customer_name, recent.order_date, recent.amount FROM customers c CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT order_date, amount FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS recent ORDER BY c.name

test_cases.description: 5 customers each with at least one order; most recent order per customer — 5 rows

hints: The LATERAL subquery can reference the outer table (customers) and runs once per outer row — use LIMIT 1 to get only the top result.
CROSS JOIN LATERAL behaves like INNER JOIN when the lateral subquery always returns a row; use LEFT JOIN LATERAL if some customers may have no orders.
explanation: The LATERAL subquery SELECT ... FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1 runs once per customer row, fetching only their latest order. Alice's latest: 2026-02-01 (320.00). Bob's latest: 2026-01-20. Carol: 2026-02-05. Dave: 2026-02-10. Eve: 2026-03-01. Total: 5 rows. Without LATERAL this would require window functions or a correlated subquery in the WHERE clause.
